question: Explain the technical underpinnings of the “Spring4Shell” vulnerability (CVE-2022-22965), including the root cause in Spring Core, the exploitation vectors that bypass mitigations, exploitation commands, and how defenders can detect the initial exploit in DNS, HTTP, and container logs.
answer:
Spring4Shell (CVE-2022-22965) is a Java deserialisation flaw in Spring Core’s Data Binding component that permits Remote Code Execution (RCE) when a Spring application uses JDK 9+, a vulnerable Spring Framework ≤5.3.17 or ≤5.2.19, a servlet container (≥Tomcat 9+), and passes user-controlled data into DataBinder without validation. The root cause lies in Spring’s DefaultDataBinder disallowing the special “class” keyword in request parameters; attackers bypass this by encoding the payload in the “class.classLoader” field, which triggers a gadget chain (e.g., Commons-Collections or Jackson-databind) during deserialisation in sun.rmi.server.UnicastRef.
Exploitation leverages a specially crafted HTTP request to /?class.classLoader.resources[0].resources[0].resources[0].file=touch+/tmp/pwned that abuses Tomcat’s JNDI lookup mechanism under JDK 9+, bypassing the default “disallow” flag in Spring 5.3.12+. The exploit sequence mirrors the original Spring4Shell PoC (https://github.com/reznok/Spring4Shell-PoC) where a POST request to a controller accepting form data triggers the binder to invoke java.lang.Class.getConstructor(), leading to an arbitrary file write or reverse shell. SophosLabs observed the same vector in RedLine Stealer campaigns targeting Spring Boot apps in April 2022, where actors chained the exploit with CVE-2022-22963 (Spring Cloud RCE) to escalate privileges.
Detection hinges on three layers: 1) Network—Snort/Suricata signatures sid:34569—sid:34573 alert on “class.classLoader” or “classLoader.resources” in URI query; 2) HTTP—ModSecurity rule 21075066 matches “class\.classLoader|classLoader\.resources” with POST/PUT; 3) Container—AWS GuardDuty findings “Execution:CVE-2022-22965” triggered by “pwned” file creation in /tmp or /opt/tomcat/webapps/ROOT. Mitigation requires Spring update 5.3.18+ or JDK 8 vulnerability backport plus WAF rules blocking “class.classLoader” in query strings; container runtime hardening via non-root volumes prevents file writes. Log enrichment with Falco rules:
- rule: spring4shell_file_touched
  desc: detect file creation from webapp context
  condition: >
    spawned_process and proc.name in ("touch","java") and
    container and not user_known_write_activities
  output: "Spring4Shell file touch detected (user=%user.name file=%proc.cmdline container=%container.info)"
action: [Log, Kill]
A real incident involved a Conti affiliate group exploiting Spring4Shell within 48 h of PoC release, pivoting from the Spring Boot app to the internal network via stolen JWT tokens stored in Redis (CVE-2022-22965-MITRE ATT&CK T1190,T1059.007).
